systemic_fix: Make every account's exit and every new member visible. Two rules. (1) Nobody joins a client chat without a named ALTR person introducing them in that chat, saying who they are and what they'll touch. Anyone who asks for a login or code without that introduction is removed. This week a vendor nobody introduced got a live 2FA code and logged in. (2) When a client gives notice, the owner opens an exit ticket the same day with four lines: acknowledgement sent, final statement issued, access handed back, credentials rotated. It stays on the dashboard until all four are done. Five of six churned clients have at least one of those still open, three of them for over a month. Under both sits the same fix as every run: one named owner per account, a weekly written status with a real number, and every promise either closed in writing or declared dead out loud. follow_through is 3.00 on all eighteen accounts for the third straight run, and it will stay there until promises are tracked somewhere other than the chat.
team_broadcast:
Team — two things, effective today.

FIRST: nobody new joins a client chat without being introduced in that chat by one of us. Name, what they do, what they'll touch. If someone asks a client for a login or a code without that introduction, they come out of the chat and you tell me. This week someone we never introduced asked a client for a 2FA code in the group, got it, and logged in. Three weeks ago we told every client not to share codes with anyone, including us. We can't keep sending the opposite message.

SECOND: when a client tells us they're leaving, their owner tells me within the hour and opens an exit checklist the same day: (1) a personal acknowledgement, (2) a final statement with real numbers, (3) access handed back, (4) passwords rotated. No collection messages to a departing client until I've signed off on the final figure. Right now we have clients who left a month ago and are still waiting on all four.

And the standing rule: if you say 'I'll check' or 'I'll update you', you post the answer within 24h or say out loud that it isn't happening. Tagging someone else doesn't hand it off. It's still yours until they answer.

The good news is real: the weekly leak report and Melissa's repost updates got thank-yous from clients who'd gone quiet. That's what clients notice, so keep it going.
pattern: We are fast and we are liked, and that still isn't the problem. The new data point this week is that visible, concrete work wins clients back almost immediately: Liza, Mila, Sarah Lloyd and Sarah all re-engaged within days of getting something specific (a dated repost update with the account list, a weekly leak report, a real call). What loses them is the same as ever. A promise goes out by @-tag, nobody owns it, and it lapses without anyone deciding it should. The six exits all followed the same request answered several times with a holding reply, a call offer or 'solved', and never with a number. Exits are the pattern's worst case, because nothing on our side stops when a client leaves except the talking.
